title: Letter Formation Families
keyIdea: Small letters can be put into families by the first move the pencil makes. Ladder letters (l, i, t, u) start at the top and pull straight down. Curly c letters (c, a, d, g, o, q) start like c: just below the middle line, curling back over the top to the left. Robot letters (r, n, m, h, b) pull down, go back up the same line, then over. Zigzag letters (v, w, z) slant down and up. No small letter starts at the bottom. Practising one family at a time trains one movement, and the family is set by the first move, not by how tall the letter is: d is tall but is a curly c letter.
familyTip: Practise one family a day, big and then small. Draw letters with a finger in the air, on the table, then on paper. Say the move as you go: c letters say 'curl back over the top', robot letters say 'down, up and over'. If your child starts at the bottom, put a green dot where the pencil should start.

visual.caption: Which family is each letter in? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: tap where each letter starts, drag its first move, sort letters into four families and spot letters made the wrong way.

kid: Every letter starts in one place. Your pencil goes down there first. Small letters start at the top, not the bottom.
Some letters start with the same move. We call them a family. l, i and t are ladder letters. You pull down, like going down a ladder.
c, a, d, g and o are curly c letters. Start like c. Curl back over the top, to the left.
n, r, m and h are robot letters. Go down, back up the same line, then over. v, w and z are zigzag letters. d is tall, but it starts with a c, so it is a curly c letter.
adult: Ages 5 to 6. The national curriculum for England asks Year 1 pupils to form small letters the right way. They start and finish in the right place. They also learn which letters belong to which handwriting families, the letters formed in similar ways, and practise them. Many UK schemes call the families long ladder, curly caterpillar, one-armed robot and zigzag monster. Some put e, s and f with the curly letters and k and p with the robots, so match your child's school.

Families matter because the hand learns one move, not 26 shapes. Once c is secure, a, d, g, o and q are c plus one more line. Robot letters share the move 'down, back up, over', which helps later with joining. On writing lines, small letters like a and n start near the dashed middle line.

Common mistakes: starting at the bottom and pushing up; going round o, a or c the wrong way, like a clock, which makes joins hard and can lead to b and d mix-ups; starting d with its stick instead of its c; sorting by height, so h or d gets called a ladder letter; and lifting the pencil halfway through a robot letter.

In the lab your child taps the start dot on six letters and watches each one grow. Next they drag the first move of six letters and are told if the curl goes the wrong way. Then they sort twelve letters into four families, find the odd one out in five rows, and check six letters for a bottom start or a wrong-way curl.

practice.prompt: Which letter is in the same family as c?
practice.hint: Which one starts with a curl back over the top?
practice.explain: o starts just like c and curls back to the left, so it is a curly c letter. l pulls straight down and n goes down, up and over.

practice.prompt: Kim writes {n} rows of the letter a. Each row has {k} letters. How many letters a does she write?
practice.explain: {n} rows of {k} make {=n*k} letters. Each a starts like c, then adds a line down.

practice.prompt: Where does the pencil start for t?
choices: At the top of the line
practice.hint: t is a ladder letter. Which way does a ladder letter go?
practice.explain: t is a ladder letter, so you start at the top and pull down. The cross comes last.

practice.prompt: A family has {a} letters. You practise {b} of them today. How many are left for tomorrow?
practice.hint: Take the letters you did today away from the whole family.
practice.explain: {a} take away {b} leaves {=a-b} letters to practise tomorrow.

choices: robot: down, back up and over
practice.hint: After the pencil goes down, does it stop or go back up?
practice.explain: n goes down, back up the same line, then over the hump, so it is a robot letter.

pool.prompt: d has a tall stick. Which family is it in?
pool.hint: Think about the first move, not how tall it is.
pool.explain: d starts with a c curve, then the tall stick. The first move picks the family, so d is a curly c letter.

pool.prompt: Which way does o go round?
choices: Back over the top, to the left
Over the top, to the right
pool.hint: o starts in the same place as c. Which way does c curl?
pool.explain: o curls back over the top, to the left, just like c. Going the other way is a common slip.

pool.prompt: Which group is all one family?
pool.hint: Do they all start with the same move?
pool.explain: c, a and g all start like c. l is a ladder letter, and n and v are in other families.

pool.prompt: Ben starts his l at the bottom and pushes up. What should he do?
choices: Start at the top and pull down
pool.hint: Do any small letters start at the bottom?
pool.explain: l is a ladder letter. Start at the top and pull down. No small letter starts at the bottom.

pool.prompt: Why do we practise r, n and m together?
choices: They start with the same move.
They are next to each other in the ABC.
pool.hint: What does the pencil do first in each one?
pool.explain: r, n and m all go down, back up and over. Practising them together trains that one move.

pool.prompt: There are {a} ladder letters and {b} zigzag letters on a card. How many letters is that?
pool.hint: Put the two families together and count.

pool.prompt: Which letter is the odd one out: l, t, i, o?
pool.hint: Three of them pull straight down.
pool.explain: l, t and i are ladder letters. o is a curly c letter, so it is the odd one out.

pool.prompt: Ava writes {n} robot letters each day for {d} days. How many robot letters does she write?
pool.explain: {n} × {d} = {=n*d} robot letters, like n, r and m.

pool.hint: v slants down to the line, then back up. Which family does that?
pool.explain: v slants down to the line, then up again, so it is a zigzag letter, like w and z.
